findings.root_cause: Calibration was captured with --tier esp32_ht40_192 (192-subcarrier baselines), but enrollment was run with --tier ht40. BaselineCalibration::deviation() for an Ht40 baseline accepts both 192 and 128 subcarrier frames, and for 128 it uses only the first 128 bins — so 128-subcarrier frames were compared against 192-subcarrier baselines, inflating presence_z for Node2/Node4.
findings.note: Node2/Node4 baselines have much smaller per-subcarrier std (median ~1) than Node1/Node3 (~3-3.6); with AMP_STD_FLOOR=1e-12, small RF shifts become large z. Baseline amplitude also drifted +4..+5 units between calibration and empty enrollment.
findings.next_step: Re-run multi-node enrollment matching the calibration tier: OPENBLAS_SYSTEM=1 cargo run -p wifi-densepose-cli -- enroll --all-nodes --baseline-dir ./baselines/roomB --output-dir ./enrollments/roomB-test --tier esp32_ht40_192. Then enforce baseline subcarrier count in enroll so a 192 baseline never consumes 128 frames.

live_path_session_2026_09_12.summary: The pose-fusion UI served by the bundled sensing server stayed on watermarked SYNTHETIC data while three ESP32-S3 nodes were streaming CSI at ~30 fps each. Three independent defects were found; the governed trust path was stripping the per-node raw amplitude vectors on 45.9% of live cycles (privacy demotion), the UI treated such a stripped cycle as a verified live frame, and the page's WebSocket port guess (httpPort+1) never matched the bundled server (HTTP 8080 / WS 8765).

chain: ContradictionFlag::TimestampMismatch fires when the spread of the newest per-node frame timestamps exceeds config.soft_guard_us (default 20000 us)
node_frames_from_states_with_guard falls back to host-arrival time when mesh time is unavailable, which is the case for plain CSI-over-UDP nodes
3 nodes each emitting one frame per ~30 ms give a newest-arrival spread that is roughly uniform over one frame interval, so a 20 ms soft guard sits at the median
demoted=true -> effective_class Restricted -> EngineBridge::suppress_raw_outputs() true -> main.rs publishes amplitude: [] and subcarrier_count: 0

measured.status_endpoint_alternation: effective_class flipped Anonymous <-> Restricted about once per second with demoted true/false in step

root_causes.fix: start the sensing server with WDP_SOFT_GUARD_US=55000 (existing override; hard guard stays at 60 ms and the upstream invariant stagger < soft_guard_us < guard_interval_us still holds)
root_causes.upstream_follow_up: IMPLEMENTED in PR #1911 commit e2331154: trust.demotion_reason + trust.demotion_count on /api/v1/status, plus a WARN on the first demotion (later ones rate-limited to one per 30 s)

root_causes.detail: Array.isArray([]) is true, so an amplitude-stripped cycle still called _markVerifiedFrame() and the buffers were blanked to zeros, showing 0.00 while isLive was already true
root_causes.fix: require ampArr.length > 0 before decoding, keep the last verified frame when a cycle carries no decodable CSI, move the RSSI/presence refresh into _updateSensingMetadata

root_causes.detail: the page guessed ws://<host>:<httpPort+1>/ws/sensing (Docker 3000->3001); the bundled server serves HTTP+UI on 8080 and the sensing WebSocket on 8765, so the guess resolved to 8081 and connectLive() failed silently
root_causes.fix: reuse the SENSING_WS_PORT_BY_HTTP_PORT table from ui/services/sensing.service.js ({'3000':'3001','8080':'8765'}), keeping httpPort+1 only as the fallback

wire_verification.conclusion: the IQ payload reaches the server complete and untruncated; the later empty amplitude is a publish-time privacy mapping, not a parse or wire problem

root_causes.detail: the endpoint reported the global s.vital_detector, which only the simulator paths feed; the live ESP32 path feeds the per-node NodeState::vital_detector and mirrors only the smoothed result into s.latest_vitals

root_causes.detail: the detector was tuned to csi_fps_ema, which counts grid-rejected arrivals too (38-47 Hz here) while the detector consumes only accepted frames (~7-21 Hz), so window capacities were about 2x too large
root_causes.fix: a second EMA over accepted frames only, surfaced as accepted_sample_rate_hz

root_causes.detail: any >20% move of the rate estimate retuned the detector and cleared its history, and the estimate swings with bursty arrivals even when the clock is unchanged
root_causes.fix: a change must persist across 25 consecutive mutually consistent evaluations (RATE_CHANGE_CONFIRMATIONS)

root_causes.detail: the remaining wipes were real: the grid-gated arrival rate genuinely moves between ~7 and ~21 Hz over seconds (capacities 212, 430, 441, 544, 554, 625 at a 30 s window), so no rate estimate can stabilise it and the spectra need a uniform clock
root_causes.fix: resample: one detector sample per fixed 100 ms period holding the newest accepted frame (zero-order hold), detector configured for 10 Hz once

breathing_window_progression.why: the confidence is an FFT peak-to-band-mean ratio over a 0.4 Hz-wide band, so it grows with the number of in-band bins; the metric is window-dependent by construction and that is documented in the code rather than hidden

calibration_policy.persistence: a finalized runtime calibration is NOT persisted; a restart returns /api/v1/calibration/status to `none`
calibration_policy.bootstrap_route: POST /api/v1/calibration/bootstrap/promote does store a privacy-reduced image, but a restored image is deliberately a bootstrap prior with negative-only authority (field_model.rs: 'A restored image is only a bootstrap prior'), and explicit_calibration_fresh_at is false whenever bootstrap_baseline_active — so promoting does not keep the vitals gate open
calibration_policy.duration_600_s: FieldModelConfig::min_calibration_duration_s documents why it is not padding: slow environmental variation (HVAC cycles, thermal drift) can only be observed over time, however fast the nodes stream (#1756). 0 disables it for tests only — not a convenience knob

expiry.implication: a calibration taken in the evening covers that night; the next evening needs a new one

invalidates_a_calibration: a different node set or a node moved (source_node_ids are frozen into the binding)
a different subcarrier grid (the binding freezes one grid)
a channel change (the earlier 2412 -> 2462 MHz move) or an AP change
a room layout change (the field model hashes mesh geometry at calibration time)
a server restart, since the model is not persisted
calibration_policy.recommendation: keep per-session calibration as the default. It fits sleep monitoring naturally: the room is empty for the 10 minutes before bed, and a calibration taken then is Fresh for the whole night. Persisting a runtime calibration is a real feature worth doing, but it changes a trust rule, so it belongs in its own reviewed change (store the privacy-reduced snapshot on finalize, restore it on startup, and authorize it only while it is within its freshness window AND the current background still matches the stored reference).
calibration_policy.note: roomB is not the bedroom; the bedroom setup will invalidate any baseline anyway, so persistence buys little until the room is final

activity_result.conclusion: the next change is not another threshold: activity must be derived from residual-energy dynamics (short-window versus long-window variation) rather than from the amplitude-jitter features, and the quiet-floor EMA must only learn from conformance-confirmed-quiet periods

vitals_result.conclusion: the heart-rate VALUE remains untrustworthy without a reference sensor; the gate publish rate is ~9.5% of frames because confidence hovers at the threshold

fixes_applied_before_this_test: the noise margin was applied twice (score and scaled thresholds) and made motion undetectable - removed from the score
runtime_background_match: the field model's empty-room conformance check now also gates a calibration collected in this process, with negative-only authority

no presence claim during baseline warm-up, plus a MOTION_NOISE_FLOOR_PRIOR of 0.03, because a zero floor collapsed the threshold onto its 0.04 fallback and an empty room reported present_still 12 s after a restart

agc_measurement_2026_09_13.question: Upstream issue #1804 reports the receiver AGC rescaling CSI in discrete gain steps (per-frame mean amplitude 10..290 within one node at constant RSSI). Is that what suppresses our motion features too?
agc_measurement_2026_09_13.method: 9 minutes, empty room, 91555 frames sampled from the live WebSocket at ~170 frames/s aggregate; per frame and per node: mean/min/max of the published amplitude vector, that node's RSSI, and the frame-to-frame mean-amplitude ratio
agc_measurement_2026_09_13.conclusion: AGC is NOT the dominant problem on this array: the amplitude scale is stable to within ~1.4x and frame-to-frame ratios sit on 1.0, unlike the 29x swing reported upstream. The motion features are therefore suppressed by something else, which the same session identified: smoothed motion ran 0.041-0.064 empty versus 0.010-0.061 walking (no separation), while the calibration residual energy moved 3-4x (4.2-13.7 -> 18-41).

secondary_observations.node2_large_steps: 404 frame pairs (1.3%) move more than 20%, the only node with such steps
secondary_observations.node3_rssi_swing: 24 dB RSSI span while its amplitude stays within 1.26x - a propagation or association change, not a gain change; worth watching on that node

next_approach: derive activity from residual-energy dynamics (short-window versus long-window variation) instead of amplitude-jitter features
gate the quiet-floor EMA on conformance-confirmed-quiet periods, because it currently absorbs presence (it learned 0.283 while a person was in the room, raising the threshold to 0.85)
